text: twisting his limbs. One moment he was kicking toward the shape in the ceiling, lungs burning, hands scraping slick surfaces. The next, he was alone. Water above. Water below. No direction. No light. No grip. The water crawled into every seam of skin and clothing like a living thing. It pulsed in Dwight’s sinuses, hissed in his ears, beat against his ribcage with an endless roar. Panic surged. Dwight’s lungs seized. He forced himself not to inhale, not to kick too hard. He stayed close to the ceiling, one hand pressed flat against it, working along by feel alone. Plaster. Tile. Seam. Crack. Pipe— Nothing. Every sound dissolved into the water, tunneling awareness into vague thumps and creaks just out of range. A thud rolled through the water, metal on metal, distant. He twisted, bubbles clawing free from his throat. Another vibration, swallowed so fully it was more pressure than sound, rippling along his ribs. It might’ve been David. Might’ve been the pipes screaming again. He couldn’t tell. A pipe materialized where the hallway shouldn't have had one, catching his shoulder and spinning him partway around. He found the ceiling again and reoriented, except he wasn't certain anymore which direction he'd come from. The current pushed at his legs from a new angle. Something moved in the water nearby — too large to be debris, too deliberate — and grazed the back of his calf with the particular patience of something that had been following him for a while. Dwight kicked hard, arms scrabbling against walls that weren’t where they should be. His brain screamed up! but his body spun, panic shredding orientation until he didn’t know which way he was moving. The flashlight had been a compass, however weak, and now it was gone. Pressure gnawed at his ears. His chest locked, ribs straining for breath that wasn’t there. His vision prickled at the edges, the rising stars of a blackout dancing with every frantic movement. Something brushed past his leg again. Not a graze this time. Not the lazy curious arc of something circling. This was deliberate — a solid nudge against his calf that sent a shock of pure animal panic up his spine, and his body reacted before his brain could intervene. He jerked, twisting, bubbles tearing from his nose in a strangled choke, and for one disorienting heartbeat, he was sure there wasn’t a surface. Just water forever. His knuckles struck tile. Then hit a ridge. Broken ceramic. Something hard and sharp and... right. He clawed upward, fingers catching, dragging. His arms caught the edge of something, and he pulled. Up. Up. Some kind of splinter tore skin from his palm. His whole body surged, slamming shoulder-first into the gap. The world detonated. His throat ripped open around the first savage gasp, water and air fighting for space. He broke the surface gagging, hacking, shuddering so hard his knees buckled the instant he scrambled onto the sodden tiles. He curled onto his side, heaving, spit and floodwater streaming out of him in trembling bursts. He coughed until his ribs ached. Pressed his forehead to the floor. Breathed. The hallway was dark and quiet except for the soft lap of water against the edges of the hole behind him. Just the water. Just his shaking breaths. Dwight allowed the cool tiles to hold him, boneless, limbs jittering with aftershock. Relief hit sharp and dizzying; he’d found it, he was out, he was alive. He allowed himself to simply breathe against the cold tiles for a time. It took a minute to realize he was the only one doing so. He twisted back toward the hole, horror seizing his gut like a vice. "...David?" The sound cracked, raw, too small for the drowned dark. Nothing answered but the slap of water against ceiling. The tile was cold against his palms and his chest heaved and the water ran off him in thin streams and he waited for the sound of David breaking the surface behind him. Hands finding the edge. The grunt of effort. Something. The water lapped softly at the edges of the hole. It hadn’t even been that long, but David wasn’t there. The water churned quietly below him, but no head broke the surface. No splashing. No sign. His head buzzed from the pressure knotting in his chest. David had been right there. Right beside him. One selfish beat, he thought of staying out, curling in the puddle and pretending David would follow. His body screamed for it. He'll be right behind you. The thought came with the exhaustion, easy and warm and almost convincing. Just rest. Just breathe. He's coming. Dwight lay on the tile a moment more and breathed and listened to the silence. Then moved back to the hole. He found it by feel, fingers trailing across tile until the edge dropped away, and reached into the water up to his shoulder. Nothing. He swept his arm in a slow arc, searching, hoping to catch a fistful of sleeve, hair, something. Anything. The gentle tug of the current wrapped around his wrist, providing nothing in return. A swirl of movement shifted gently against the back of his hand and he leaned further in, focusing on the current. It wasn’t the same kind of tug on his skin. This felt focused — a deliberate movement rather than the flow that had knocked him around in the hallway. David’s close — Dwight realized in an instant — but he’s off course. The same current that tried to steal Dwight is dragging David too, just far enough to miss the exit. He was lost. The silence of the hallway pressed in expectantly. Like the floor was holding its breath, waiting to see if he’d move. Dwight swore he could hear the distant tick of settling tile, the whisper of water threading under the walls.
